rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet calls prayer without Umm al-Qurʾān deficient and tells a Persian worshipper to recite it silently, even behind the imam.
rows.anchor: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ، يَقُولُ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits a qudsī report in which God divides al-Fātiḥa between Himself and the servant; the declaration of worship and plea for help is shared, and God grants what is asked.
rows.anchor: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The same report assigns the servant’s request for the favored path, away from those under wrath and those astray, to the servant; God grants what the servant asks.
rows.anchor: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو موسى
rows.claim: Ḥiṭṭān reports that a congregant declared prayer established through piety and almsgiving; Abū Mūsā recalled the Prophet’s rule to follow the imam, say amin after 1:7 for God’s answer, and mirror the imam’s movements.
rows.anchor: صلى بنا أبو موسى فلما كان في القعدة دخل رجل من القوم فقال أقرت الصلاة بالبر والزكاة

rows.speaker: نعيم المجمر
rows.claim: Nuʿaym reports that Abu Hurayra recited the basmala and al-Fātiḥa in prayer, said amin after 1:7, and was echoed by the congregation; he affirmed his prayer resembled the Prophet’s.
rows.anchor: عَنْ نُعَيْمٍ الْمُجْمِرِ، قَالَ صَلَّيْتُ وَرَاءَ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ فَقَرَأَ

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s instruction to say amin when the imam reaches 1:7; whoever’s amin coincides with the angels’ is forgiven for previous sins.
rows.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s command to say amin after the imam recites 1:7, promising forgiveness of past sins when the worshipper’s response matches the angels’.
rows.anchor: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ

rows.speaker: وائل بن حجر
rows.claim: Wāʾil b. Ḥujr’s father reports that the Prophet raised his hands below his ears at the opening takbir and said amin after reciting 1:7.
rows.anchor: عَنْ عَبْدِ الْجَبَّارِ بْنِ وَائِلٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ صَلَّيْتُ خَلْفَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said twelve angels hurried to carry a worshipper’s abundant, good, blessed praise, and nothing stopped it before it reached the Throne.
rows.anchor: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو موسى
rows.claim: Abū Mūsā reports that the Prophet taught worshippers to say amin after the imam recites 1:7, so God answers them.
rows.anchor: سَمِعَ أَبَا مُوسَى، قَالَ إِنَّ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم خَطَبَنَا وَبَيَّنَ لَنَا سُنَّتَنَا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet directs worshippers to follow the imam’s takbirs, bowing, and prostration, which the imam performs before them; they answer his praise with a prayer for God’s praise.
rows.anchor: قَالَ نَبِيُّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When seated, worshippers should begin with al-taḥiyyāt, salutations, and the testimony; the Prophet calls these seven words the greeting of prayer.
rows.anchor: قَالَ نَبِيُّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd transmits that the Prophet taught the sermon of need: praise, seeking help, forgiveness and refuge, the testimony of faith, then three verses including 4:1, 3:102 and 33:70.
rows.anchor: عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān flags disconnections: Abū ʿUbayda did not hear from his father, and he names ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAbd Allah and ʿAbd al-Jabbār b. Wāʾil as similarly unlinked.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبد الرحمن أبو عبيدة لم يسمع من أبيه شيئا ولا عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jarīr reports that the Prophet addressed needy arrivals, recited 4:1 and 59:18, and urged everyone to give what they could, even half a date; companions brought food and clothes.
rows.anchor: سَمِعْتُ الْمُنْذِرَ بْنَ جَرِيرٍ، يُحَدِّثُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ كُنَّا عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: After an Anṣārī led the donations, the Prophet taught that whoever begins a good practice in Islam receives its reward and the reward of those who follow, while a bad precedent carries their sins too.
rows.anchor: فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ مَنْ سَنَّ فِي الإِسْلاَمِ سُنَّةً حَسَنَةً فَلَهُ أَجْرُهَا وَأَجْرُ مَنْ عَمِلَ بِهَا

none: The phrase ‘ما منعك’ appears in an unrelated report about Abu Bakr leading prayer; it does not quote 7:12.
The phrase ‘بني آدم’ occurs in an unrelated report about prayer, omens, and a slave girl; it does not discuss 7:172.
The mention of ‘بني آدم’ is incidental in a report about a horse’s dawn supplication, unrelated to 7:172.
The request for forgiveness and the Prophet’s reply are not connected to 12:92; the wording only coincides.
This report about Jewish questioners and the nine signs does not discuss or quote 18:37.

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: ʿAlī reports the Prophet’s prostration prayer: he submits to God, whose creation and fashioning of the face, hearing, and sight culminate in the verse’s praise of God, the best of creators.
rows.anchor: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Jābir b. ʿAbd Allāh reports a similar Prophetic prostration supplication, praising God as the best of creators after affirming God fashioned the face and gave it hearing and sight.
rows.anchor: عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ يَقُولُ فِي سُجُودِهِ

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Muḥammad b. Maslama reports that during voluntary night prayer the Prophet used this prostration supplication, affirming God as Lord and praising Him as the best of creators.
rows.anchor: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ إِذَا قَامَ

none: This report concerns the reward for following a funeral; it has no connection to 28:81.
This report concerns voluntary prayer after the night prayer and does not discuss or quote 28:81.

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that Abū Ḥudhayfa adopted Sālim and arranged his marriage; before the revelation, adopted sons were publicly treated as biological sons and inherited from their adopters.
rows.anchor: عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، أَنَّ أَبَا حُذَيْفَةَ بْنَ عُتْبَةَ

words: ٱدْعُوهُمْ لِءَابَآئِهِمْ هُوَ أَقْسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: الله
rows.claim: The revelation directs Muslims to identify adopted children by their fathers; when a father is unknown, they remain brothers in religion and mawālī rather than biological sons.
rows.anchor: حَتَّى أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ فِي ذَلِكَ ‏{‏ ادْعُوهُمْ لآبَائِهِمْ هُوَ أَقْسَطُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ
